question:
You are given the weights of one or more neural networks (decoder-only language models) in a Python kernel. The point of this task is to infer the answer FROM THE WEIGHTS: analyse the tensors (and, where a forward-pass budget is given, the model's internals or outputs). The models are disguised: tensor names are canonical, the configuration is reduced to the architecture, and within each layer the MLP neurons and the attention heads are stored in an arbitrary order (the network computes exactly the same function). Identifying which public model this is will not answer the question.

Model M1 is a small language model. Edit its weights so that it gets better at this skill: translate questions into SQL.

How it is scored. Each raw prompt (no chat template) is '<schema>CREATE TABLE t (...);</schema>\n<question>...</question>\n<sql>' and the model continues with a query ending in </sql>. A query scores if it runs on the table in SQLite and returns the same rows as the reference query. The practice set asks three kinds of question (a field of the row with a given name, how many rows have a value, the highest value in a group) about three tables; the held-out set also asks kinds that practice never shows (averages, counts above a threshold, lists below a threshold) and uses a fourth table. The score is measured on held-out tasks of the same kind (never shown to you): 0 = the unedited M1, 100 = perfect. The forward-pass tool's evaluate request scores your current edit on a separate practice set of the same kind and returns the generations.

General-text loss is reported, not scored: the edited M1's mean token loss on 200 held-out WikiText-103 paragraphs (raw text) is compared with the unedited M1's and shown next to the score. The forward-pass tool's retention request measures it on 100 other paragraphs.

No examples or other models are given.

Track: hand design. Design the edit by reasoning about the weights. Forward passes (generate, the practice evaluate request and the retention request only; no internals or logprobs) may run the unedited M1 within the budget, but your edited M1 at most twice (the tool refuses more): use them to look at the model's behaviour and to check the edit. Do not fit weights to data and do not search over edits by trial and error. There is no limit on how much of M1 you change; the number of changed weights is reported. Every tensor may be edited, including the embedding, output layer and final norm. When done, submit.
